conclusion: Factor −16 did not produce the requested coherent refusal-to-answer switch on any of the five active prompts. The qualification denial remained explicit; four other active responses had malformed openings. The inactive ordinary symptom control was unchanged.
interpretation: −8 was a pilot cutoff, not a demonstrated limit. This matched extension shows that doubling the tested negative factor to −16 still did not yield the requested switch for L19–T368 on these prompts. Several outputs contain generic advice, which is different from fulfilling requests for diagnosis, personalized treatment, or a prescription; some clean responses already supplied generic information. The feature often first activates on the already-generated "cannot" token. These results do not establish a selective safety/refusal control mechanism and do not determine what other strengths or features would do.
assessment_method: Manual reading of all 24 complete visible outputs. Separate qualification denial, requested-task fulfillment, generic guidance, and malformed wording. No clinical correctness assessment; no safety metric derived from wording regex.
